summary: Well‑executed, preregistered paired emulation study comparing an LLM‑only arm to a generate–validate–repair (GVR) arm under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Execution artifacts are archived and reconcile to a null (zero‑difference) outcome because every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator and no repairs were invoked. The manuscript is scientifically honest about this outcome and provides useful design lessons for future NetOps evaluations, but a few presentation and disclosure fixes are required before finalisation.
critical_issues: References / citation-format: the manuscript bundle lists cited-record identifiers (DOI/arXiv URLs) but the submitted paper must include a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography with full bibliographic metadata (authors, title, venue, year) and IEEE‑style numeric in‑text citations. This is required by the venue and by the review guidelines and can be resolved using the archived verified bibliography records.

Runtime sampling disclosure: model_configuration.json records temperature=null. Per the preregistration and reviewer requirements, the manuscript must explicitly state the recorded sampling parameters (temperature, top_p, seeds) or state that the provider returned unset values and point to the archived per-call sampling metadata (path and SHA‑256). A clear sentence in Methods and in the Disclosure Statement is required clarifying that null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling and that per-call sampling metadata are archived.

Confirmatory inference limitation must be explicit and prominent: because n10=n01=0 (no discordant pairs) the preregistered primary test cannot provide evidence that GVR reduces unsafe applies; the manuscript must explicitly state that the primary confirmatory hypothesis is untestable in this execution (not simply “not supported”) and quantify the realized implications for detectable effect size given the observed baseline rate. This clarification must appear in Methods/Results (not only in Discussion).
required_revisions: Replace the current References section with a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography (authors, title, venue, year) and ensure in‑text citations use IEEE numeric markers; verify each cited record supports the proximate claim (use the archived verified-record list).

Add an explicit statement in Methods and in the Disclosure Statement referencing execution/model_configuration.json (provide its archived path and SHA‑256 already present in the bundle) that temperature was recorded as null/unset, that null≠zero determinism, and that per‑call sampling metadata (provider traces/seeds) are archived at the listed execution/provider_calls path (include the path and representative hash from the manifest).

In Methods or Results add a concise, explicit statement that the primary paired test produced zero discordant pairs (n10=n01=0), explain the statistical consequence (primary test is uninformative for a reduction claim in this execution), and report the realized implication for detectable effect (e.g., state that with observed baseline rate=0 the study cannot demonstrate a positive reduction and provide the corresponding upper bound/interpretation using archived analysis outputs).
optional_revisions: Shorten and tighten the Disclosure Statement text so it remains complete but avoids duplicating execution-log detail; keep the mandatory master_prompt locator and SHA‑256 prominently.

Add a short table or sentence giving the realized minimum detectable effect or an upper bound on unsafe‑apply rate for each arm given observed data (if such a calculation is present among archived analysis artifacts, include the exact artifact path/hash).

Strengthen the Discussion with concrete examples of task/adversary types or verifier‑coverage classes that would be needed to produce verifier‑failing initial candidates, perhaps linking to specific archived representative tasks that were validator‑passing to illustrate contrast.
